pages.title: Chairman's Message
pages.subtitle: A message from the Chairperson of the Board
pages.seoTitle: Chairman's Message — Imperial Securities Company Limited
pages.seoDescription: A message from Chairman Bhaktiram Ghimire of Imperial Securities Company Limited.
pages.body:
Dear Valued Investors,

Warm greetings from Imperial Securities Company Ltd. On behalf of our team, I'm thrilled to connect with a wider audience through our updated website. While we've consistently strived to keep our esteemed customers informed across various channels, this fresh endeavor marks a significant milestone in our commitment to you.

Established in 2011, Imperial Securities Company Ltd. stands as a prominent stockbroking firm and wealth management entity headquartered in the prime location of Anamnagar, Kathmandu. Our unique retail-focused stock trading model, providing revolutionary platforms and expertise, caters to a diverse clientele. As proud members of the Nepal Stock Exchange Limited (NEPSE) and registered Depository Participant (DP) with CDS and Clearing Limited (CDSC), we aim to secure a lasting reputation and trust among our existing and potential clients in the stock broking business arena.

Investing in the stock market has proven highly lucrative, even in markets like Nepal's. However, we acknowledge the stress investors might face due to a lack of timely and proper intermediary services. Hence, our aim is to shoulder the best responsibility towards stakeholders, ensuring our clients receive assured professional services promptly.

We envision ourselves as a family of honest, loyal, and dedicated professionals, leveraging technology, innovation, and a personal touch to ensure high member satisfaction and goodwill. Understanding that the progress and prosperity of our investors are the keys to our success, we've embarked on a journey to bring the best national and international practices and technologies to Nepal, benefiting all stakeholders collectively. Our recent memberships in the Association of National Numbering Agencies (ANNA) and the International Organization of Securities Commissions (IOSCO) signify recognition for Nepalese stock markets in the international arena, providing us with expanded opportunities ahead.

Imperial Securities embodies core values such as proficiency, innovation, and a relentless commitment to serving our customers and stakeholders. As the Chairperson of the Board, it's my privilege to lead this distinguished stock broking company. We take pride in being among the top five most trusted stock broking companies in Nepal and aspire to ascend as the market leader in the near future. Our clients, partners, and shareholders are our true assets, and I extend heartfelt gratitude to the Ministry of Finance, the Office of the Company Registrar, SEBON, Nepal Rastra Bank, NEPSE, CDSC, our auditors, legal advisors, and all other entities for their unwavering guidance, support, and contributions on our journey thus far. A special mention to our dedicated staff for their invaluable contributions.

Together, let's strive for eminent success through our unwavering joint efforts in the days to come.

faqs.question: How to open a DEMAT and Meroshare account with Imperial Securities?
faqs.answer:
Step 1: Visit Our Website 
Go to our official website: 
👉 https://imperialsecurities.com.np 

Step 2: Apply Online 
From the top navigation bar, click on “Apply Online” and select the DEMAT option.

Step 3: Complete the Online Form 
Fill in all required details accurately and upload the necessary documents as instructed.

Step 4: Make Payment 
Pay the DEMAT account opening charge of NPR 200 via eSewa or Khalti . 
✔️ The DEMAT account is valid for 1 year .

Step 5: Video Verification Scheduling 
After submitting the form, book a convenient date for video verification . Our team will call you on the scheduled date to complete the verification process.

Step 6: Submit Your Application 
Review your information and click Submit to complete the application process.

faqs.question: How much time does it take to open a DEMAT account ?
faqs.answer: Once your application, payment, and video verification are completed, our team will verify your details and activate your DEMAT and MeroShare accounts . You will get email notification on same day.

faqs.question: What is a DEMAT account?
faqs.answer: It is an electronic account where your shares are stored digitally.

faqs.question: Is PAN mandatory?
faqs.answer: PAN is mandatory for investors whose total share transaction exceeds NPR 5 lakh.

faqs.question: What is a broker account (Trading Account)?
faqs.answer: A broker account, also known as a trading account, is an account opened with a stock broker like Imperial Securities Company Limited that allows you to buy and sell shares on the Nepal Stock Exchange.

faqs.question: How can I open a broker account (Trading Account)?
faqs.answer:
You can open a trading account with Imperial Securities Company Limited in two easy ways:

🌐 Online Method:

- Visit our official website

- Click on “Apply” 

- Select “TMS Registration” 

- A new page will appear where you can view the required documents 

- Click on “Click Here to Register” 

- Fill out the online form and submit your application

🏢 Offline Method:

Or, you can visit our office with the required documents and our team will assist you in opening your account manually.

faqs.question: What is a stock broker?
faqs.answer: A stock broker is a licensed intermediary who executes buy/sell orders on the Nepal Stock Exchange on behalf of investors.

faqs.question: Is the stock market regulated in Nepal?
faqs.answer: Yes, it is regulated by the Securities Board of Nepal.

faqs.question: What are brokerage charges?
faqs.answer: Charges vary based on transaction size as per NEPSE guidelines. Click here to know the charges

faqs.question: What is IPO?
faqs.answer: IPO (Initial Public Offering) is when a company offers shares to the public for the first time.

faqs.question: What is the minimum amount to invest?
faqs.answer: You can start with as low as NPR 1,000 depending on share price.

faqs.question: What is secondary market trading?
faqs.answer: Buying and selling shares after they are listed on NEPSE.

faqs.question: Is stock market investment risky?
faqs.answer: Yes, prices fluctuate based on market conditions, company performance, and economic factors.

faqs.question: How do I choose good stocks?
faqs.answer: Choosing good stocks requires a combination of fundamental analysis, market understanding, Techincal analyisi and patience .

faqs.question: What is Margin Trading?
faqs.answer:
Margin trading is a facility where investors can buy shares by paying only a part of the total amount , while the remaining amount is financed by the broker.

If you want to buy shares worth NPR 1,00,000:

- You may pay only NPR 30,000 (initial margin)

- The broker finances the remaining NPR 70,000

faqs.question: How long does it take to settle a trade?
faqs.answer: Settlement is typically completed within T+2 days (2 working days after trade).

faqs.question: When do I receive money after selling shares?
faqs.answer: Funds are usually credited within 2–3 working days.

news.body:
कृपया यथाशीघ्र EDIS प्रक्रिया पूरा गर्नुहोला। अन्यथा नियमअनुसार २०% जरिवाना लाग्न सक्छ। 

👉 कृपया MERO SHARE मा Google / Chrome / Safari / Web Browser मार्फत मात्र Login गर्नुहोस्। ❌ Mobile App प्रयोग नगर्नुहोस्। 

1️⃣ My Purchase Source मा जानुहोस् र WACC Calculate गर्नुहोस्। ➡️ My Purchase Update गर्दा WACC Rate कति आएको छ भनेर अनिवार्य रूपमा Check गरेर मात्र Update गर्नुहोस्। 

2️⃣ My Purchase भित्र गएर → My Holding Update गर्नुहोस्। ℹ️ नोट: यदि तपाईंले बेचेको कम्पनी Merger भएको छ भने " Update गर्दा “ User Defined Merger Flag” मा Click गर्नुहोस्। ➡️ Remarks मा “ Merger” लेख्नुहोस्।" छैन भने, यो Step Skip गरेर अगाडि बढ्न सक्नुहुन्छ। 

3️⃣ My EDIS भित्र गएर → Transfer Share मा Click गर्नुहोस्। ➡️ View Details Click गर्नुहोस् ➡️ Select All मा Click गर्नुहोस् ➡️ त्यसपछि Update र Confirm गर्नुहोस् 

✔️ हरियो Highlight मा “ Successfully Transfer for Requested Share” देखिएपछि तपाईंको EDIS सफलतापूर्वक पूरा भएको मानिन्छ।

blog.title: Mutual Fund- A Boon Or A Bane In Nepalese Context
blog.excerpt: A mutual fund is a financial intermediary that pools the savings of investors for collective investments in a diversified portfolio of securities. A fund is said to be mutual as all of its returns, minus its expenses…
blog.body:
A mutual fund is a financial intermediary that pools the savings of investors for collective investments in a diversified portfolio of securities. A fund is said to be mutual as all of its returns, minus its expenses are shared by the fund investors. A mutual fund serves as a link between the investor and the securities market by mobilizing savings from the investors and investing them in the securities market so as to generate returns. Thus, a mutual fund is a kin to Portfolio Management Services (PMS). The government of Nepal has made mandatory provisions to allocate 5% of the total initial public offerings(IPO) for mutual funds. The mutual fund plays a vital role in the securities market and has its own importance/benefits.

Mutual funds in Nepal are a relatively new investment option, but they have quickly become popular among investors. Some of the major reasons for this include Professional management, Portfolio Diversification, Reduction in transaction costs, transparency, affordability, liquidity, Convenience and flexibility, and so on.

- Professional management: 

An average investor lacks the knowledge of capital market operations and doesn't have large resources to reap the benefits of investment. Hence, one requires the help of an expert. It is not only expensive to “hire the services of an expert” but much more difficult to identify the real expert. Mutual funds are managed by professional managers who have the requisite skills, knowledge, and experience to analyze the performance and prospectus of companies. They make possible an organized investment strategy, which is hardly possible for an individual investor.

- Portfolio Diversification: 

An investor undertakes risks if one invests all of his funds in a single script. Mutual fund invests in a number of companies across various industries and sectors. This diversification reduces the riskiness of the investments. One doesn't invest in a mutual fund but rather invests through a mutual fund. Thus one can invest in diversified sectors with a small fund as low as Rs.1000, where s/he gets 100Units of Face Value Rs.10.

- Reduction in transaction costs: 

Compared to direct investing in the capital market, investing through mutual funds is relatively less expensive as the benefits of economies of scale are passed onto the investors.

- Liquidity: 

Often, investors cannot sell the securities held easily, while in the case of mutual funds, they can easily encash their investment by selling their units to the fund if it is an open-handed scheme or selling them on a stock exchange if it is a close-ended scheme.

- Convenience :

Investing in mutual funds reduces paperwork, saves time, and makes investment easy.

- Transparency: 

Mutual funds are highly regulated and transparent investments. Investors can easily track detailed information about the fund's holdings, performances, and fees. Performances can be easily traced through their NAV(Net Assets Value). NAV per share can be obtained by dividing net assets( total market value of assets minus liability ) by the number of shares or units outstanding.

blog.title: NEPSE: The Game of Narrative
blog.excerpt: NEPSE is a game of narrative; and story. If we vividly remember the good old days of the 2020-21 bull market, the rise from 1100 to 3200 was a complete narrative game. Liquidity plays a vital role, let's keep this…
blog.body:
NEPSE is a game of narrative; and story. If we vividly remember the good old days of the 2020-21 bull market, the rise from 1100 to 3200 was a complete narrative game. Liquidity plays a vital role, let's keep this thing aside and focus on the narrative. Narratives are influenced by market makers to the public.

Stocks are not traded in the market, narratives are traded. Narrative drive to speculation and speculation drive to unsustainable rally (unhealthy growth) of the price. 

Case studies 1: Hydropower 

Hydropower is generally small-cap in nature. There is a lockup period for 3 years of promoters meaning they (promoters) can't sell for a minimum of 3 years. Low paid-up capital equates to less supply in the market, anywhere from 2-3 big whales can absorb major supply easily creating artificial scarcity of supply that led to a pump in stock price. What boosted its rally was the news of right shares. The price of the stock that proposed the right share was about 400-500% on average. Some of the stocks even did 10x. 

Case studies 2: NRIC 

NRIC, issued IPO to the public during the pre-COVID, listed in mid-COVID, and rallied post-COVID. The only licensed approved reinsurance in Nepal, the government had heavily invested, once it is successful in collecting premiums from foreign countries, it is the next big thing. The narrative was slowly building the hype cycle of NRIC. They never used to update their quarterly reports in time. Since it collects premiums from other countries, the paid-up capital was too small for NRIC, so the right share was imminent. This narrative drove the price from Rs 500 to Rs 2000, the right share was never announced and now this stock is trading at Rs 629 as of writing.

Case studies 3: RBCL 

One of the funniest rallies I have ever seen in the capital market since I joined was in RBCL. 

A company with paid-up capital of only Rs 26 crore, but this is very small for a non-life insurance company because as per the insurance board, the minimum requirement for a non-life insurance company was a minimum of Rs 1 arba at that time (now 2.5 arba). So the only possible way for RBCL to increase their paid-up was through bonus shares. A government-owned company, very old, had an enormous amount of assets to its name which can easily pass bonus shares. Hyping up the narrative again, the stock rallied from Rs 10k to Rs 25k. It topped in May 2021, as of October 2023, no notice of bonus shares has been announced and the stock price is Rs 13-14k per share. Accumulate, make stories, spread stories, sell stories. That's how it is played right?

Case studies 4: NTC 

A mature strong fundamentally sound company NTC is a government-backed company with a whooping 91% stake meaning very less floatable shares in the tradable market. Never in its operational life, has the company ever announced any kind of bonus or right shares. But this is a bull market, the story is “traded” not the “stocks”. Any kind of story, from minor to major, any story is sold in this bull market and I am pretty sure some sort of new narrative will be formed in future upcoming bull markets as well. The rumor around every corner from social media to group chat, NTC is about to make its debut bonus share announcement was roaming around for quite some time. As expected, the price rallied from Rs 1000 to Rs 1800. The strange thing here is, this rally happened after the market topped out in August 2021. The rally started in October 2021 and topped out in February 2022. When NTC proposed bonus shares, it became the top of its individual cycle and the stock price hasn’t recovered to date.
